title: The Product and Service Lifecycle and the Value Chain

header.html: The ITIL Product and Service Lifecycle (10%)
List the eight lifecycle activities; understand the lifecycle; understand that the activities are not sequential or linear and can be used iteratively; define the value chain
the official ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus, version 5.0 (February 2026), categories 3.1 and 4.4.1

html:
1The eight activities

The ITIL Product and Service Lifecycle is a model of eight activities that apply to every product and service:

Discover → Design → Acquire → Build → Transition → Operate → Deliver → Support

Activity One-line idea
Discover Find out what consumers need and what is possible
Design Turn needs into specifications and prototypes
Acquire Get the people, tools and components needed
Build Create, configure and test the product or service
Transition Move it safely into live use
Operate Run it so it performs as agreed
Deliver Provide the service to consumers
Support Restore normal operation and help users
Exam tip

. The list has eight items, in this order. A common distractor is an ITIL 4 word such as plan, improve or engage; those belong to the old six-activity service value chain.

2Not sequential, not linear

The activities are not a waterfall. Work loops, overlaps and repeats: a support finding can send you back to discover or design, and teams may run several activities in parallel. Use them iteratively, a little at a time, with feedback.

Not every organization performs all eight: a provider that builds nothing still discovers, transitions, operates, delivers and supports. [Verify live]

Leaning Activities
More product work discover, design, acquire, build
The bridge transition, operate
More service work deliver, support

Products and services are two sides of the same digital solution, so the lifecycle covers both.

3The value chain

The value chain is the operating model of the lifecycle activities: the flow of activities that an organization performs to turn demand into value through products and services. It is one of the five components of the ITIL Value System (Module 8).

Old wording In ITIL 4 the service value chain had six activities: plan, improve, engage, design and transition, obtain/build, deliver and support. Version 5 simplified this and uses the eight-activity lifecycle. If a question names the six old activities, it is using ITIL 4 language. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. The lifecycle is not a waterfall. Any option that says the activities must be completed once, in strict order, is wrong.

Exam tip

. Count eight. If an option lists six activities with words such as plan or improve, it describes the ITIL 4 value chain.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which list shows the ITIL Product and Service Lifecycle activities?

  • APlan, improve, engage, design and transition, obtain and build, deliver and support
  • BDiscover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver, support
  • CDiscover, plan, build, test, release, support
  • DDesign, build, test, deploy, monitor, retire
Show the answer

Answer: B. Option A is the ITIL 4 value chain; option B is the Version 5 lifecycle.

S2Which statement about the lifecycle activities is CORRECT? (1) They are not strictly sequential. (2) They can be used iteratively. (3) They must always be completed in order, one at a time. (4) They apply only to physical goods.

  • A3 and 4
  • B1 and 3
  • C1 and 2
  • D2 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: C. The activities are not sequential or linear and can be iterated.

S3A managed service provider builds no software but runs and supports a client's platform. Which statement fits?

  • AIt performs none of the lifecycle activities
  • BIt must still perform all eight in strict order
  • CIt is outside ITIL
  • DIt performs only the activities that apply to it, such as transition, operate, deliver and support
Show the answer

Answer: D. Not every organization performs every activity.

S4Identify the missing word(s). Products and services are [ ? ] of the same digitally enabled solution.

  • ATwo competing versions
  • BSeparate owners
  • CTwo layers of contract
  • DTwo sides
Show the answer

Answer: D. ITIL treats them as two sides of the same solution.

S5An engineer finds a defect in live support and the team revisits the design. What does this show?

  • AThe lifecycle activities can loop back and be used iteratively
  • BThe lifecycle is a straight line
  • CThe support activity is not part of the lifecycle
  • DThe design activity is finished forever
Show the answer

Answer: A. Activities can loop and repeat.

S6Which activity sits between "build" and "operate"?

  • ADiscover
  • BAcquire
  • CTransition
  • DSupport
Show the answer

Answer: C. The order is build, transition, operate.

4.2 Recall questions

R1How many lifecycle activities are there in Version 5?

Show the answer

Eight.

R2Name the eight activities in order.

Show the answer

Discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver, support.

R3Are the activities strictly sequential?

Show the answer

No; they are not sequential or linear and can be used iteratively.

R4What did ITIL 4 call the six-activity flow?

Show the answer

The service value chain.

R5Which activity restores normal operation and helps users?

Show the answer

Support.

R6What is the value chain?

Show the answer

The flow of activities that turns demand into value through products and services.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Eight activities discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver, support
Shape not sequential or linear; iterative
Product / service lean discover-build / deliver-support; transition and operate bridge
Old wording six-activity ITIL 4 service value chain
